authoring: blind — authored from clone reads only, no retrieval run; every expect clause grep-verified (whitespace-normalized substring) in the named file; queries re-scoped to chapters that actually exist in the curriculum after the prior suite assumed non-existent on-call/incident-response material

school-of-sre.shape_risk: No large-file risk (103 md files under courses/ total 692,115 B; biggest is level101/security/network_security.md at 43,460 B) — the dilution risk is per-topic fragmentation into intro/key_concepts/further_reading/conclusion files where intros and conclusions are 0.2-2 KB stubs, and much of the bulk of the substantive files is pasted console output (SHOW REPLICA STATUS dumps, dig/tcpdump transcripts) rather than prose.

queries.q: In semi-synchronous MySQL replication, what happens to a transaction on the primary before control returns to the session?
queries.expect: a commit performed on the primary host is blocked until at least one replica acknowledges it

queries.q: What advantage do realtime signals have over standard signals when the same signal is sent to a process more than once?
queries.expect: If multiple instances of a realtime signal are sent to a process, then the signal is delivered multiple times

queries.q: In a messaging system, what happens to poison pill messages instead of them just being thrown away?
queries.expect: Instead of discarding problematic messages, they are redirected to a DLQ, allowing engineers to analyze and resolve the issues

queries.q: Under the hood, what actually is a branch in git?
queries.expect: Branch names (human readable) are pointers to those commits in the tree

queries.q: We changed a DNS record to retire a backend server — when is it actually safe to shut the server down?
queries.expect: the servers can be removed from the pool only after waiting till TTL post the changes are made to DNS records
